ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: During the Industrial Revolution, because of the production and deposition of large amounts of dust and smoke around cities and factories, many insect species underwent major changes. One of the most famous examples is the peppered moth population. Researchers counted the numbers of peppered moths and Longtail Moths per square kilometer in 8 different urban environments in 1802, and repeated the experiment 100 years later in 1902. Why was it also necessary to investigate the Longtail Moth population?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Longtail Moths were included in the investigation as a control, because they were expected not to undergo obvious changes due to the changes related to the Industrial Revolution.

raw_record.original_question: 在工业革命期间，由于城市和工厂周围大量灰尘和烟雾的产生与沉积，许多昆虫物种发生了重大变化。最著名的实例之一是斑蛾种群。研究人员在1802年对8个不同城市环境中每平方公里的斑蛾和长尾飞蛾（Longtail Moths）数量进行了统计，并在100年后的1902年重复了该实验。为什么还要对长尾飞蛾种群进行调查？
raw_record.answer: Longtail Moths were included in the investigation as a control, because they were expected not to undergo obvious changes due to the changes related to the Industrial Revolution.

White-bodied peppered moths were high in number in 1802, about more than thirty, and by 1902 clearly decreased to single digits; black-bodied peppered moths were low in number in 1802, and by 1902 clearly increased to more than thirty. In contrast, the bar heights for Longtail Moths in 1802 and 1902 are almost the same, both around more than thirty, and the numbers are basically stable. Combined with the information in the question stem that the Industrial Revolution caused dust and smoke deposition and that the research focus is changes in the peppered moth population, it can be inferred that the researchers investigated Longtail Moths in order to provide a reference object: if the number of Longtail Moths basically does not change with industrial pollution, they can serve as a control, helping to judge whether the changes in the number and body-color proportions of peppered moths are indeed related to the environmental changes brought by the Industrial Revolution, rather than all moths undergoing the same overall change.
